subject: Renewal restructure — laddered consumption, auto-renew opt-in & burn smoothing
messages:
From: Jamie Lee <jamie@crestline.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal timing + ask on smoothing overages

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for the 2028 term is coming up (July 15). We’ve been tracking steady growth in inference usage and want to discuss a move from an annual committed model to a 3‑year laddered consumption commitment: gradual ramp in Year 1 -> stronger commit in Year 3.

Two asks on our side:
- Can Redwood provide a credit buffer or burn‑smoothing mechanic for Q3 to Q4 as we onboard a second product line?
- Is there an opt‑in for auto‑renew on a yearly cadence inside a multi‑year agreement (so we can lock current pricing but retain flexibility)?

I attached our last quarter usage export for reference. Procurement (procurement@crestline.ai) is on cc to coordinate contractual steps.

Thanks,
Jamie Lee
Head of ML Platforms
Crestline Data
Attachment: Crestline_Usage_Report_Q1.csv (CSV, 87KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
To: Jamie Lee <jamie@crestline.ai>
Cc: procurement@crestline.ai, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + ask on smoothing overages

Jamie — thanks for the note and for the usage file. This is right in our wheelhouse.

High level thoughts:
- We can structure a 3‑year laddered commitment (1yr ramp -> 2yr steady -> 3yr floor + burst) with embedded annual checkpoints.
- For Q3->Q4 smoothing, we typically propose a short‑term credit bucket (one‑time, non‑recurring) to absorb onboarding overages while you reach steady state. That can be amortized across Year 1 pricing.
- Auto‑renew: we do offer an opt‑in clause that auto‑renews annually within a multi‑year master amendment, with a customer notice period for opt‑out (e.g., 60 days). Pricing protection can be preserved for the agreed term.

I’ve looped in Karthik (AM) to review technical traffic patterns and Kimberly (billing) to sketch pricing mechanics. Can we set a 30‑minute call Wed 6/6 at 10:30am PT to walk through a concrete amendment and credit sizing?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com
To: Jamie Lee <jamie@crestline.ai>, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodai.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + ask on smoothing overages

Jamie — quick technical context ahead of Wed’s call.

Looking at the CSV, your median request length and burst profile indicate a strong night‑time cadence and a weekday spike correlated with product releases. For a laddered commit we recommend:

- Year 1: 60% of current run‑rate as committed baseline, with a 25% one‑time onboarding credit to smooth Q3/Q4 spikes.
- Year 2: 110% of current run‑rate as committed baseline.
- Year 3: 150% of current run‑rate with an option to add 20% burst allocation at a discounted overage rate.

Operational notes: we can enable prefix caching for your most common prompt families to reduce effective billable tokens during ramp, which will materially lower the credit required.

I’ll bring sample telemetry and a model mapping doc to the call.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: (will share telemetry PDF on call)

From: Jamie Lee <jamie@crestline.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com
Cc: procurement@crestline.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + ask on smoothing overages

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. Quick clarifying Qs for the call:
1) The 25% onboarding credit — is that applied as a one‑time invoice credit or as a preloaded token credit applied against usage?
2) For Year 3 burst discount, can you share example math vs standard overage? Procurement wants a simple table to review.

If you can circulate a short amendment draft and a pricing table before the call, that will speed approval on our side.

Jamie

From: kimberly_park@redwoodai.com
To: Jamie Lee <jamie@crestline.ai>, marissa_cole@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com
Cc: procurement@crestline.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + ask on smoothing overages

Jamie — attaching a first‑pass amendment (Proposed_Amendment_v2.pdf) and a one‑page pricing table for the laddered commit and burst tiers. Answers inline:

1) The 25% onetime onboarding credit can be structured either as an invoice credit applied after month end or as prepaid usage credit. We usually recommend prepaid token credit when customers want immediate runway.

2) Example math (simple):
- Standard overage: $0.08 per 1k tokens
- Year 3 burst discounted overage: $0.05 per 1k tokens (applies to burst allocation above committed floor)

We’ve modeled a blended annual price that amortizes the onboarding credit across Year 1, showing net effective unit price month‑by‑month. See the attached PDF.

I’ll bring a redlineable DocuSign draft to the call.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Revenue Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Proposed_Amendment_v2.pdf; Pricing_Summary_Laddered.xlsx (XLSX, 32KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwoodai.com
To: Jamie Lee <jamie@crestline.ai>, kimberly_park@redwoodai.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com, rishi_malhotra@redwoodai.com
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + ask on smoothing overages

Great sync today — thanks everyone. Notes/next steps from the call: 

- Crestline confirmed intent to convert to the 3‑yr laddered commitment with the onboarding credit route (prepaid token credit of 25% applied at contract effective date).
- Action (Redwood): Kimberly to send a DocuSign amendment with auto‑renew opt‑in language (60‑day opt‑out), amortized credit schedule, and explicit burst discount table.
- Action (Redwood): Karthik to deliver telemetry-backed caching plan and expected token reduction estimate by Friday 6/8.
- Action (Crestline): Procurement to confirm internal PO cadence; Jamie to share final headcount ramp plan that maps to predicted Year 2 traffic.

Rishi, I looped you in for visibility on ARR impact and escalation if legal needs to weigh in on auto‑renew language.

Please reply all with any corrections. I’ll attach the final DocuSign when Kimberly issues it.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
